J1.basis: This SaaS pivoted from "InboxZap" (email cleanup tool) to "Lumina" (AI meeting assistant)... The GSC export confirmed it: all query/impression data is for email/Gmail terms totally unrelated to a meeting assistant, and the only real traffic is ~17 clicks/month on the old brand name "inboxzap"
J1.rationale: Explicitly names the pivot, treats GSC email data as legacy, ties it to live-site reality, and frames every fix around the meeting-assistant positioning. Falls just short of a 10 only because the repo-staleness framing is implicit.

J2.basis: 301-redirected the 12 off-topic posts to `/blog` instead of letting them 404 or keep ranking for irrelevant queries
J2.rationale: Applies a single blanket disposition (all 12 → /blog) justified only by aggregate 'thousands of impressions, near-zero clicks' rather than per-asset or tiered decisions citing individual impressions/positions; no harvest/repurpose or successor-specific redirects.

J3.basis: Added a quiet "(formerly InboxZap)" footer note to bridge brand equity for the residual branded searches... build the meeting-assistant cluster as the growth engine
J3.rationale: Avoids both failure modes: doesn't chase inbox content, doesn't torch equity (redirects rather than 404s, preserves branded search via footer, builds new cluster). Weakened by redirecting to a generic /blog rather than sequencing a transition into topically relevant successors.
